requirements.title: Passing a procedure designator as an actual argument does not execute it unless execution is needed
requirements.definition: The appearance of a procedure designator as an actual argument does not constitute a reference to that procedure unless such a reference is necessary to complete the specification of the actual argument.

pending.procedure-actual-not-executed-by-passing: Pass a module function bomb as an actual procedure to a subroutine whose dummy procedure is never called; initialize a module marker to -3 before the call and assert it remains -3 afterward, while bomb would set it to 99 before returning 5.
pending.procedure-actual-executed-by-call-contro: Use the same actual function bomb with a companion subroutine that calls its dummy procedure once; assert the marker changes from -3 to 99 and the returned integer is 5, making the noncall facet load-bearing.

accounting.rationale: The paragraph defines data-object and procedure reference events separately.
A data object is referenced when its value is required during execution. 9.2, 10.1.4, 10.1.11, 10.1.12, and specific statement owners govern contexts requiring values.
A procedure is referenced when executed. Function/subroutine reference and invocation plans are registered in Clause 15.
The actual-argument exception separates data-object value reference from procedure execution as an actual argument.

A data object designator appearing as an actual argument is not automatically a value reference; actual-argument association and specification needs are owned by Clause 15 and expression/specification-expression catalogues.
